context_documents.title: 2022-125 · Impact-resistant acquisition and reduced spin require coordinated contacts
context_documents.body:
# 2022-125: Impact-resistant acquisition and reduced spin require coordinated contacts

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A wide dead-axis collector feeds a curved S-path and hooded launcher with powered upper contacts to reduce backspin. The interview discusses planned bouncing-cargo improvements and future climb automation, while the filmed climb remains manually sequenced.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source explicitly identifies fast acquisition and impact resistance as collector priorities.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A controlled transfer can prepare incoming speed/spin, but each curve introduces another compression interface. Planned Velcro and planned automation must remain unfielded at this snapshot; neither can be used to explain its existing results.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test side impacts, bouncing entry, full-path current and manual climb timing before attributing later automation benefits.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers 125 NUTRONs | Rapid React
source_reviews.review_basis: Read timestamped English transcript of team members at Week Zero.
facts: Pneumatic intake uses a dead axle and metal printed pulleys. Retraction actively pushes cargo into the feeder. The S-curve preserves a low robot and leaves an open path for bouncing cargo.
Light grippy main wheels, two powered contacts and adjustable hood support range and backspin control. The climb uses contact against another rung to change hanging attitude.
Full climb automation, a five-ball auto and the Velcro bounce-pickup roller were plans at the interview.
limitations: Automatic transcript contains inconsistent ordinal descriptions of the rungs. The reaction principle is clearer than the exact sequence.

source_reviews.title: 2022 FRC125 Reveal — The NUTRONs present Freefall
source_reviews.locator: March 11, posts 1 and 9 by Brandon Holley
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the team’s reveal and explanatory follow-up in the indexed thread.
facts: Sorting was added after Week Zero. Once two desired balls are held and the inner feed stops, arriving cargo exits through the top of the intake. The team credits Citrus as an influence.
limitations: No sensor placement, software or exact path dimensions are given. The team’s rules interpretation is not an official ruling.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Freefall pairs a low, open-front cargo system with a two-contact adjustable shooter. Its intake deploys briefly for acquisition and then retracts to complete the transfer. The early climb is a rung-reacting traversal mechanism that changes chassis pitch during the hang to make the final hooks reachable. The March sorting system adds a distinct way for surplus cargo to escape upstream of the launcher.
source_review.piece_flow: With the collector down, the roller gets the first purchase on floor cargo. As the collector retracts, its roller pushes the ball into the feeder contact, accelerating the first handoff. The S-curve connects that low entrance to the hooded launcher while leaving a possible route for balls bouncing above the normal floor intake. The shooter applies powered contacts to control both velocity and spin. In the later sorting account, stopping the inner feed when two desired balls are staged leaves a top-of-intake ejection route. Exact Week Zero staging sensors and March color-dependent routing through the lower path remain unresolved.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Collector angle changes entry and transfer geometry, so stow timing is part of cargo handling. The offset between low entrance and raised shot is covered by a curved feeder. On the climb, the hanging angle governs the final hook reach. Pushing on another rung rotates the suspended chassis, making the field contact a load-bearing interface rather than a timing cue.

subsystems.name: Intake and entrance
subsystems.construction: Pneumatic retracting collector with dead axle, metal printed pulleys and a separate roller identified for prospective Velcro.
subsystems.operation: Deploys near a ball and retracts essentially immediately to push it into the next roller.
subsystems.team_rationale: Fast acquisition and resistance to hits were priorities. Prototypes suggested Velcro could capture low-bouncing cargo otherwise missed.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Retraction can increase handoff force without another actuator, but the two contacts must overlap in time. A late retract can leave cargo riding at the bumper.
subsystems.interfaces: Floor contact, retraction stroke, feeder inlet and open upper entry.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect dead-axle supports and handoff gap after side impacts. Test bounced and grounded balls separately.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller diameters, dead-axle bearing stack and later Velcro installation.

subsystems.name: Feeder and March sorter
subsystems.construction: S-shaped roller path. Later sorting architecture provides an ejection path through the intake.
subsystems.operation: Moves cargo through the low package to the shooter. Once two desired balls are held, stopped inner feed allows incoming cargo to be ejected above the intake.
subsystems.team_rationale: Low height and open front drove the curve. Hunting for alliance cargo in mixed piles took too much time at Week Zero.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An alternate exit can save the approach turn and a shooter cycle. The release path must stay clear with a worn or partially compressed ball already staged.
subsystems.interfaces: Retracting collector, curved feeder compression, desired cargo count and shooter inlet.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure whether a rejected ball disturbs either held ball. Check surfaces for wedging at changes in curvature.
subsystems.unknowns: Sorting sensor type, lower exit geometry and command sequencing.

subsystems.name: Launcher and range control
subsystems.construction: Light grippy wheels, powered front and rear contacts, adjustable hood and Limelight.
subsystems.operation: With the hub in view, software adjusts hood and shooter settings. Team favored the edge of the tarmac.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior wheels gave useful grip at lower weight. Tests favored reduced spin and enough energy to enter without bouncing out.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The two contact speeds jointly determine energy and spin. A faster shot can reduce successful retention even if it enters the opening more often.
subsystems.interfaces: Feeder output, traction, vision range and hood angle.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare first and second exit conditions, then check for tread slip and hood backlash.
subsystems.unknowns: Wheel construction details, setpoint curves and chassis aim routine.

subsystems.name: Rung-reacting climber
subsystems.construction: Primary deployment arms, reaction bars and final capture hooks.
subsystems.operation: After initial engagement and pull, reaction bars press on an intermediate rung to flatten the robot enough for the final hooks to catch traversal. Week Zero sequencing was manual after arm deployment.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team sought a faster route that skipped an intermediate hang and added the reaction bars after finding an unfavorable hanging angle.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The extra contact changes pitch and local rung load. One-sided contact can twist the chassis and leave one hook short.
subsystems.interfaces: Initial suspension, reaction contact and final hook capture.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test loaded skew, contact slip and recovery after a missed final catch.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact rung ordinals from a corroborating diagram, actuator details and later automation deployment.

revisions: Week Zero interview establishes early manual climb and no active sorting. March reveal follow-up establishes later ejection behavior. Five-ball and automated climb were future work at the earlier snapshot.
transferable_principles: Use a deployment mechanism for handoff where its controlled sweep can maintain contact. Measure hub retention as well as entry, and design the loaded reach geometry before committing the climber.
disconfirming_conditions: Retraction-assisted transfer is weaker if multiple balls block the same throat. The pitch reaction works only if intermediate contact stays stable across setup errors.
remaining_gaps: Chassis drive model, event-specific sorting revision, full sensor state machine and verified climb contact sequence.

recommended_images.purpose: Seek stills showing retraction handoff and the rung reaction contact.
